title: a test that runs alone or skips with no condition

explain.what: A test runs alone ({ only: true }, test.only(...)) or skips with no condition (skip: true / skip: 'a reason', it.skip(...), @pytest.mark.skip, @unittest.skip, a bare Rust #[ignore]).
explain.why: With only, the runner runs that test and silently skips the rest; a skipped test checks nothing. The suite still looks green.
explain.fix: Fix the test, or delete it if it no longer applies. If it must skip on some machines, make skip a condition (for example the platform: skipif in Python, cfg_attr in Rust); a Rust test that only runs on demand says why: #[ignore = "..."].

js.message: a committed { only: true }: the rest of the suite stops running
a skip with no condition: make skip a condition, or fix the test
a committed .only( or .skip(: the rest of the suite stops running, or the test checks nothing

py.message: a skip with no condition: use skipif with a condition, or fix the test

rs.message: a bare #[ignore]: say why (#[ignore = "..."]), or fix the test
